The multiple-chain release gives sampling arguments the same meaning across
`posterior_samples()`, `fitted_samples()`, `smooth_samples()`,
`derivative_samples()`, their `add_*()` helpers, and coefficient draw functions.
Obsolete arguments now produce errors with migration guidance. Controls must
be named; only the model, or the data and model in `add_*()` helpers, can be
passed by position. This prevents old positional calls from changing meaning.

## Draw counts and evaluation points

`n_draws` always means the total retained draws across all chains. It must be
divisible by `chains`. Generating draws requires an explicit count: the previous
defaults ranged from one draw to 10,000 draws. `chains = NULL` uses one chain,
or infers the chains from supplied coefficient draws.

| Previous argument | Replacement |
|:------------------|:------------|
| `n` in fitted, posterior, predicted, smooth and coefficient sampling | `n_draws` |
| `n_sim` in derivative sampling | `n_draws` |
| `n` in derivative sampling | `n_grid` |
| `n_vals` in smooth sampling | `n_grid` |
| `object` in derivative sampling | `model` |
| `object` in `add_*()` sampling helpers | `data` |
| `freq` | `frequentist` |
| `newdata` | `data` |
| `ncores` | `n_cores` for MH chains; `n_threads` for Gaussian draws |
| `n_cores` for Gaussian sampling | `n_threads` |
| `term` in smooth sampling | `select` |

For example, the previous derivative call

```r
# Previous interface; now produces an informative error.
derivative_samples(model, focal = "x", n = 100, n_sim = 1000)
```

becomes

```r
# 1,000 retained coefficient draws, evaluated at 100 points.
derivative_samples(model, focal = "x", n_draws = 1000, n_grid = 100)
```

`n_grid = 200` is the common default for smooth and derivative sampling.
For smooths, it supplies the resolution to `smooth_data()`; multidimensional
smooths can contain more rows than `n_grid`. Derivative sampling constructs a
slice along `focal`, holding other variables at representative values. Explicit
`data` determine the evaluation locations instead of `n_grid`. Use explicit
`data` when the exact grid matters. Fitted and response sampling use fitting
observations when `data = NULL` and do not construct a grid.

## Multiple chains and parallel work

```r
samples <- fitted_samples(
  model, n_draws = 1000, chains = 4, n_cores = 4,
  method = "mh", burnin = 1000, thin = 1,
  diagnostics = TRUE, seed = 281
)
sampling_diagnostics(samples)
```

This retains 250 draws per chain. Every chain discards its own 1,000 burn-in
iterations; parallel chains repeat this warmup work. `thin = 2` retains every
second iteration after burn-in and still returns `n_draws` draws in total.
`n_cores` limits concurrent MH chains using mirai, capped at `chains`. An
existing worker pool is reused; otherwise temporary workers are cleaned up
automatically. Given the same seed and sampler backend, retained draws agree
between serial and parallel runs.

Gaussian sampling uses `n_threads` to control threads inside mvnfast. It does
not run concurrent MH chains. A control explicitly supplied to a method that
cannot use it produces an error, including MH controls for Gaussian draws or
Gaussian covariance controls for MH. `block_size` and `dense_limit` apply only
to `method = "mh", mh_backend = "gratia"`.

The default MH backend remains `"mgcv"`. Use `mh_backend = "gratia"` for the
compiled common-family evaluator, including independent-observation `bam`
models. The gratia evaluator rejects GAMM components; it does not evaluate
their fitted observation correlations. Both MH backends condition on fitted
smoothing, dispersion, and family parameters. `unconditional = TRUE` applies to Gaussian sampling only.

## Reusing coefficient draws

```r
betas <- post_draws(model, n_draws = 1000, chains = 4, seed = 281)
fitted <- fitted_samples(model, method = "user", draws = betas)
smooth <- smooth_samples(model, method = "user", draws = betas)
derivative <- derivative_samples(
  model, focal = "x", method = "user", draws = betas
)
```

The coefficient matrix determines the count and chain layout. Explicit
`n_draws` or `chains` must agree with it. A plain matrix without chain metadata
represents one chain; chain boundaries are never guessed from the row count.
Smooths always transform the same joint coefficient draws. The old
`rng_per_smooth` option is removed because independently redrawing each smooth
loses their posterior dependence. The previously ignored `mu`, `sigma`, and
derivative `level` arguments are also rejected.

Multiple-chain tables retain `.chain`, `.iteration`, and globally unique `.draw`
columns. Single-chain tables keep their previous columns. Attached diagnostics
refer to coefficients before transformation or response simulation.
`as_mcmc_draws()` converts coefficient matrices or sampled quantities for
posterior or coda diagnostics. Optional packages are required only when their
formats or diagnostics are requested.

## Which response sampling function to use

`fitted_samples()` draws the expected response, `smooth_samples()` draws
individual smooth contributions, and `derivative_samples()` draws derivatives.
`posterior_samples()` also simulates response variation for each coefficient
draw. `predicted_samples()` simulates responses with fitted parameters held
fixed. It uses `n_draws` for the number of response replicates and rejects
coefficient-chain controls; use `posterior_samples()` to include coefficient
uncertainty.

Model-specific capabilities still apply. For example, the native diagnostic
samplers for `lm` and mixed models support Gaussian approximations and fitting
observations only, and reject unsupported chain controls. See
`help("diagnostic_support")` for model-specific support. Functions that summarise
draws, such as `response_derivatives()` and `conditional_differences()`, keep
their existing grid and simulation-count arguments; their internal sampling
calls use this interface.
